Site Manager

Are you an experienced Site Manager who thrives on taking ownership of complex installation projects and leading teams in an international environment? Do you enjoy being hands-on while maintaining a strategic overview of project execution, customer expectations, quality, safety, and timelines? If so, you could be the Site Manager we are looking for.

As Site Manager, you will have overall responsibility for projects from the moment they are handed over by the Project Manager until successful completion on site. Acting as the senior onsite representative, you will lead multidisciplinary teams, coordinate activities across multiple disciplines, and ensure that all installation, commissioning, and testing activities are executed safely, efficiently, and according to plan.

In this role, you will work closely with Project Managers, customers, subcontractors, and internal specialists to secure a successful project delivery. You will be responsible for driving progress, allocating resources, managing budgets and forecasts, and maintaining a high level of quality throughout the installation phase. A key part of the role is building strong customer relationships and ensuring that any project adjustments are properly managed and documented.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Leading and coordinating all onsite activities, including mechanical and electrical installation, commissioning, testing, and final acceptance.

• Managing multidisciplinary site teams consisting of Site Supervisors, Commissioning Engineers, PLC Software Engineers, and WCS/WMS specialists.

• Ensuring compliance with site safety standards, quality requirements, and the company's Site Excellence framework.

• Driving planning, resource allocation, budgeting, forecasting, and schedule management for all site activities.

• Acting as the primary customer contact on site and ensuring clear communication throughout the project lifecycle.

To succeed in this role, you likely hold a degree in Marine Engineering or another relevant technical discipline and have substantial experience managing installation projects on customer sites. You combine strong technical insight with excellent leadership and communication skills and are comfortable taking full ownership of both project performance and team success.

We are looking for a proactive and decisive leader who naturally takes responsibility, remains calm under pressure, and has the ability to navigate competing priorities while maintaining focus on project objectives. Experience within warehouse automation, logistics systems, mechanical and electrical installations, and commissioning activities will be considered a strong advantage.

In return, we offer a key position in a global organization where you will play a critical role in delivering advanced automation and logistics solutions to customers around the world. You will enjoy significant responsibility, a high degree of autonomy, and the opportunity to work alongside skilled colleagues in an international project environment.

Please note that this position requires extensive international travel and long-term assignments at customer sites worldwide.

Scientific Software Engineer for Research Software Engineering Group

The European Spallation Source (ESS) is one of Europe’s largest research infrastructure projects and is building the world’s most powerful neutron source. Through cutting-edge science and technology, ESS will enable discoveries that advance our understanding of materials, energy, health, and the environment.

About the role

The Research Software Engineering (RSE) group develops and maintains critical software systems that make neutron scattering experiments at ESS possible and successful.

As a Scientific Software Engineer, you will contribute to the development of key platforms supporting the scientific user journey, including the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information systems. You will work closely with scientists, software engineers, and stakeholders across ESS to gather requirements, understand user needs, and develop robust software solutions that integrate seamlessly with the wider ESS ecosystem.

The RSE group uses modern web technologies and software engineering practices to deliver high-quality software with a long operational lifetime. In addition, the group is expanding its focus on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning solutions that can enhance the scientific user experience. As part of this effort, you will contribute to new AI-related initiatives and help establish RSE as a centre of expertise and development for AI applications within the Science Directorate.

This position is well suited for an experienced software engineer with a strong technical foundation, excellent collaboration skills, and a passion for building software that enables world-class scientific research.

Key responsibilities

• Design, develop, test, and maintain software systems supporting the scientific user journey at ESS.

• Contribute to the development of the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information management systems.

• Gather, analyse, and refine requirements from scientific and technical stakeholders across ESS.

• Design and implement integrations between RSE applications and other ESS services and platforms.

• Apply modern software engineering practices to deliver reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software solutions.

• Contribute to technical and process improvements within the SIMS group.

• Participate in AI and Machine Learning initiatives supporting the Science Directorate.

• Collaborate with scientists, software engineers, and international partners to develop innovative solutions for scientific computing and data management.

• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing within the team when appropriate.

• Contribute to software architecture discussions and technology decisions within the group.

Required qualifications

• Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

• Typically 4-7 years of relevant professional experience in software development.

• Experience developing modern web applications and services.

• Strong programming skills and experience with modern software development practices.

• Experience gathering requirements and working directly with stakeholders and end users.

• Experience designing and implementing integrations between complex software systems.

• Ability to work independently and manage technical tasks and projects with limited supervision.

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

Desirable qualifications

• Experience working with scientific software, research infrastructures, or data-intensive environments.

• Experience with cloud-based services and distributed systems.

• Experience with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning technologies and their practical application.

• Experience with user-facing platforms, portals, or information management systems.

• Familiarity with modern DevOps practices, CI/CD, automated testing, and container technologies.

• Experience working in international and multidisciplinary environments.

• Experience contributing to open-source software projects.

What we offer

DMSC is located on the DTU campus in Kongens Lyngby, north of Copenhagen, while the ESS neutron facility is based in Lund, Sweden. Together, they form a unique cross-border scientific environment in the Øresund region.

You will join a dynamic and highly collaborative international workplace with colleagues representing nearly 60 nationalities across ESS and DMSC. We offer flexible working conditions, opportunities for professional development, and close interaction between computational science, instrumentation, and large-scale experiments.

Benefits include 25 + 5 annual leave days in addition to public and company holidays, an attractive pension scheme, preventative healthcare benefits, and relocation support for international hires where applicable.

This is a full-time, permanent position based in Kongens Lyngby, Denmark, and we need someone who can start as soon as practically possible.

Learn more about living and working in Scandinavia: https://ess.eu/living-working-scandinavia

For further information

For information about the position, contact the Group Leader for SIMS, Fredrik Bolmsten at Fredrik.bolmsten@ess.eu.

For recruitment-related questions, contact Recruitment Officer Janne Erwolter at janne.erwolter@ess.eu.

Senior Data Analyst – SAP Reporting & Stakeholder Alignment

• Location: Copenhagen, Denmark or Lisbon, Portugal

• Working hours: Full-time

• Work model: Hybrid

• Contract type: Permanent

Are you passionate about turning business questions into meaningful data solutions? Do you enjoy working with stakeholders, solving complex data challenges, and transforming data into insights that drive better decisions? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

As our new Senior Data Analyst, you will join the Data & Insights team and report directly to the Head of Data & Insights. In this role, you will act as the bridge between business stakeholders and SAP data, ensuring reporting requirements are clearly defined, translated into actionable data solutions, and delivered with accuracy and impact.

You will work closely with Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Operations, and Data Engineering teams to support data-driven decision-making while improving reporting processes and data quality across the organization. This is a great opportunity to influence business decisions, collaborate across functions, and help shape the future of data and analytics at STG.

What your day will look like

In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Partner directly with business stakeholders — Finance leadership, Sales/Commercial, Supply Chain/Operations — to understand their reporting and data needs, and translate them into concrete data requirements.

• Work closely with data engineers to scope, request, and validate data pulled from SAP, acting as the translation layer between business language and technical/data specifications.

• Write and optimize SQL queries to extract, validate, and consolidate data for recurring and ad hoc reporting.

• Build and maintain Excel-based models, trackers, and reports that stakeholders rely on for decision-making.

• Consolidate data into stakeholder-ready reporting, and supporting data checks.

• Act as the go-to person for scoping ambiguous stakeholder requests — clarifying what's actually needed, managing expectations, and pushing back constructively when a request isn't well-defined or feasible.

• Identify data quality issues at the source and work with SAP module owners and data engineers to resolve them.

• Document data definitions, sources, and logic so reporting stays consistent and auditable month over month.

• Continuously look for ways to streamline the process rather than repeating manual work each cycle.

What you'll bring

• 5+ years of experience in a data analyst, business analyst, or similar data-facing role, ideally in a retail or consumer business.

• Strong SQL skills — comfortable writing and troubleshooting complex queries independently.

• Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, data modeling; Power Query is a plus).

• Familiarity with SAP data structures, particularly FI (Finance) and SD (Sales & Distribution).

• Experience with SAP Analytics Cloud (SAC), or willingness to learn it, is a plus.

• Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Business, Economics, Finance, Data/Statistics, Engineering, or related).

• Proven experience gathering requirements from business stakeholders and translating them into technical/data specifications.

• Strong stakeholder management skills — able to align multiple stakeholders (including Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, and IT/data engineering) with sometimes competing priorities, and communicate trade-offs clearly.

• Comfortable operating with a degree of ambiguity and turning it into a structured plan.

Working at STG & What to Expect

At Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG), we are so much more than what meets the eye. We combine the strength of global brands with the entrepreneurial mindset that allows people to make a real impact. Here you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, collaborate across borders, and help shape what's next.

At STG you'll find more than a role. You'll find opportunities to grow, learn from talented colleagues, and contribute to initiatives that help drive business performance across a global organization.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Ready to be part of something bigger?

Apply now and discover much more.

Our recruitment process

Before starting our hiring process, your application will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We assess each application against the key competencies and requirements for the role. If your experience and skills are a good match, you'll be invited to continue through our hiring process, which may include the following steps:

We look for the right candidate to join our team based in our Copenhagen office.

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

To support the growth of Genmab, we are looking for a Manager, Reverse logistics to join the team in Copenhagen.

As Manager, Reverse Logistics & Compliance you will develop and manage global reverse logistics processes across Genmab’s distribution network in the US, EU and APAC.

The role covers product returns, recall logistics, expired and damaged inventory, and product destruction, ensuring traceability, inventory accuracy and effective coordination with Quality, Finance and relevant compliance functions.

You will also coordinate compliance across global supply chain activities, working closely with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal and Finance to embed applicable regulatory requirements and internal controls into operational processes. This includes supporting compliance risk assessments, audit readiness, corrective actions and training, while promoting clear accountability and continuous improvement across supply chain teams and external partners.

The role reports to Director, Head of Corporate Logistics & Distribution, Commercial Supply Chain

Responsibilities

• Global reverse logistics: Establish and manage processes for return authorization, collection, transportation, receipt, segregation, inventory reconciliation and final disposition, including associated documentation and financial closure.

• Returns management: Coordinate commercial returns with 3PLs, distributors and regional teams, ensuring product eligibility, batch details, quantities, condition and supporting documentation are verified.

• Recall and withdrawal support: Lead supply chain execution of recalls and market withdrawals under the relevant governance, including collection, shipment tracking, reconciliation and operational support for mock recalls.

• Product disposition and destruction: Coordinate the execution of Quality-approved disposition decisions, including return to saleable inventory where permitted, continued quarantine or destruction. Ensure destruction is documented and reconciled with inventory and financial records.

• Traceability and systems: Maintain accurate physical and system inventory records throughout the returns lifecycle. Coordinate with IT and serialization teams on applicable product verification, serialization and traceability activities.

• Financial and trade coordination: Work with Finance, Commercial/Trade and Trade Compliance to align returns with credit processing, inventory write-offs, SOX controls and applicable customs, VAT and duty requirements.

• Performance and improvement: Develop a global scorecard covering return cycle time, reconciliation accuracy, destruction completion, supplier performance, compliance issues and cost. Lead improvements that reduce waste and strengthen process control.

• Supply chain compliance governance: Establish and maintain a global supply chain compliance framework across the US, EU and APAC, coordinating with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal and Finance to embed applicable requirements into supply chain processes.

• Compliance monitoring and remediation: Coordinate supply chain compliance risk assessments, monitor adherence to approved procedures and internal controls, and drive timely closure of, Quality events, assigned audit findings and corrective actions with accountable functions.

• Change assessment and training: Partner with Quality and compliance functions to assess the supply chain impact of regulatory and operational changes, translate agreed requirements into procedures and controls, and coordinate training for internal teams and external partners.

• Management of stakeholders: Corporate and Regional Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Commercial/Trade, Procurement, IT and serialization teams, alongside 3PLs, distributors, transportation providers and authorized destruction partners.

Requirements

jobs.occupation: Accessing orbitronics and twistronics with microscopic and ultrafast angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Physics and Astronomy programme. The position is available from February 2027 or later.

Research area and project description:

The Department of Physics and Astronomy, Aarhus University, invites applications for a PhD position, starting February 1st, 2027, offering applicants an exciting opportunity to join a new research project on orbitronics and metastable states in two-dimensional quantum materials.

The project involves fabrication of devices and their integration with the existing angle-resolved photoemission (ARPES) infrastructure at the ASTRID2 light source to discover quantum geometric effects and their link to new forms of transport phenomena.

The aim of the project is to develop new types of 2D material devices that can realize orbital, spin and valley Hall effects that form the basis for prototypical memory devices. A series of novel infrastructures will be applied to achieve these goals, including semi-automated fabrication systems in inert environments, clean-room facilities for device production, micro-focused synchrotron light for ARPES characterization at ASTRID2 as well as ultrafast femtosecond laser pulses for optical control of the materials.

The major activities include:

• Design and manufacturing of advanced 2D devices that are compatible with the microARPES experiment at ASTRID2 with the specific aim to uncover orbital-driven phenomena in materials.

• Combining synchrotron and ultrafast laser sources to visualize, excite and control electronic states with distinct orbital and spin textures in quantum materials.

• Isolation, twisting and stacking of monolayer metallic and semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenide, including materials that are sensitive to ambient conditions.

• Development of new techniques to isolate and integrate such air-sensitive materials with devices for photoemission experiments carried out in UHV conditions.

• Applying a state-of-the-art laser beamline integrated with the ASTRID2 synchrotron light source for femtosecond control of electronic structure of 2D materials.

jobs.occupation: Quantum Control of Emission in Valleytronic Materials
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Natural Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Physics and Astronomy programme. The position is available from February 2027 or later.

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a candidate for a fully funded 3-year PhD project at the Department of Physics and Astronomy, Aarhus University, in the new group of Asst. Prof. Christian Frydendahl, as part of a DFF Sapere Aude research grant.

Compact, integrable sources of circularly polarized light (CPL) are a key enabling technology for chip-scale quantum technologies, but electrically driven sources of pure CPL do not yet exist. Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) emit left- or right-handed CPL depending on which band structure valley, K or K', an electron-hole pair recombines in. Ordinarily, this occurs with an equal 50/50 split between the two valleys.

This project aims to build a new light-emitting diode geometry in which the Valley Hall effect, another intrinsic property of these materials, filters the valley index of the charge carriers during transport, enabling a purely electrically pumped source of CPL. Inducing valley polarization electrically rather than optically is one of the key open challenges in the emerging field of device-based valleytronics.

The project also includes a planned 6-month external research stay at the Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD), where you will develop and fabricate nanophotonic cavities for integration with the new diode design, enhancing its emission and CPL purity further via the Purcell effect.

Your general working tasks would be:

• van der Waals stacking of hBN-encapsulated TMDC monolayers

• Nanofabrication in the AU/SUTD cleanroom facilities (EBL, RIE, metal deposition)

• Opto-electronic characterization: probe station, polarization- and time-resolved spectroscopy at room- and cryogenic temperatures

• Publishing results and presenting at international conferences

• Participating in general dissemination and teaching activities
